subject: Cooking
title: Saturated vs. Unsaturated Fats
description: Learn Saturated vs. Unsaturated Fats in one minute.

hook.text: Butter is solid at room temperature. Olive oil is liquid. The difference is one chemical bond.

buildup.text: Saturated fats have no double bonds — their straight chains pack tightly into solid structures.

discovery.text: Unsaturated fats have double bonds that create kinks, preventing tight packing — so they stay liquid.

twist.text: Trans fats are artificially straightened unsaturated fats — the worst of both worlds for health.

climax.text: In 2018, the WHO called for global elimination of trans fats. Many countries have now banned them.

punchline.text: One bond decides if a fat is solid, liquid, or dangerous.

quiz.question: Why are unsaturated fats liquid at room temperature?
options: Double bonds create kinks preventing tight packing

details.summary: Saturated fats have straight molecular chains that pack tightly, making them solid at room temperature like butter and lard. Unsaturated fats have kinked chains from double bonds that prevent tight packing, keeping them liquid as oils.
details.whyItMatters: Fat structure determines whether a fat is solid or liquid, how it behaves when heated, and how it affects health. This knowledge guides oil selection for every cooking application.
takeaways: Saturated chains pack tightly into solids at room temperature
Double bonds create kinks that keep unsaturated fats liquid
Trans fats are artificially straightened unsaturated fats

faq.question: Why is coconut oil solid but olive oil is liquid?
faq.answer: Coconut oil is about 82 percent saturated fat with straight chains that pack into a solid at room temperature. Olive oil is about 73 percent monounsaturated with kinked chains that cannot pack tightly. The saturation ratio determines the melting point.

faq.question: What are trans fats and why are they harmful?
faq.answer: Trans fats are unsaturated fats artificially hydrogenated to straighten their chains, making liquid oils solid for processed foods. This shape lets them pack like saturated fat. They raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol, increasing heart disease risk significantly.
